chunks: From him, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Prophet or Imam), said:
When the deceased is washed, then excretes after the washing, so the excretion should be washed off, and the (whole) washing would not be repeated.
ai.seo_question: Do you need to re-wash the entire body of the deceased if they pass wind after the initial ghusl?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of partial re-purification (ghusl al-hadath) for the deceased, distinguishing between the complete ritual bath (ghusl al-janabah) and the washing of specific impurities. Shia jurists utilize this hadith to argue that the integrity of the initial ghusl remains intact unless the entire body becomes impure, thereby preventing unnecessary repetition of the ritual. This reflects the broader Shia legal methodology of distinguishing between the state of major ritual impurity and localized najasah in post-mortem rites.

en.hubeali: From him, from one of his companions, raising it, said:
‘When the deceased is washed, then excretes after the washing, so the excretion should be washed off, and the (whole) washing would not be repeated’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by certain persons of his people in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
After Ghusl (bath), if something happens, only that part is washed and repeating Ghusl (bath) is not required.’”
